subject.complex-analysis.title: Complex analysis
subject.complex-analysis.define: Holomorphic rigidity, contour methods, analytic continuation and the geometry of Riemann surfaces.
subject.complex-analysis.scope: Selected advanced-undergraduate and beginning-graduate core with advanced gateways. Entries give precise scoped statements and proof ideas, not full proofs or exhaustive courses.
subject.complex-analysis.assumed_background: Real multivariable calculus, metric limits, elementary topology and line integration.
subject.complex-analysis.learning_outcomes:
- Use Cauchy theory to derive local analyticity and rigidity.
- Choose contour, residue and zero-counting arguments with the correct domain hypotheses.
- Separate local continuation from global single-valuedness.
subject.complex-analysis.study_route: [Holomorphic functions](./notes/ca.holomorphic.md) → [Cauchy–Goursat theorem](./notes/ca.cauchy.md) → [Cauchy integral formula](./notes/ca.cauchy-formula.md) → [Power series and analyticity](./notes/ca.series.md) → [Laurent series and isolated singularities](./notes/ca.singularities.md) → [Residue theorem](./notes/ca.residues.md) → [Montel's theorem](./notes/ca.normal.md) → [Riemann mapping theorem](./notes/ca.riemann-mapping.md)

ca.holomorphic.title: Holomorphic functions
ca.holomorphic.define: Complex differentiability throughout an open set imposes strong local rigidity.
ca.holomorphic.statement: A function on an open set $U\subset\mathbb C$ is holomorphic if the complex derivative exists at every point of $U$. This is stronger than real differentiability.
ca.holomorphic.hypotheses: The derivative limit must be independent of the direction of approach.
ca.holomorphic.example: $z^2$ is holomorphic; $\bar z$ is not holomorphic on any nonempty open set.
ca.holomorphic.caution: Complex differentiability at one isolated point does not imply local holomorphy.
ca.holomorphic.prerequisites:
**From other subjects**

- [Metric limits and completeness](./notes/ra.metric.md) — Real analysis
ca.holomorphic.references:
CA: analytic functions.

- **CA** — Sigurdur Helgason; notes by Hongxi Wang. [MIT 18.112: Functions of a Complex Variable](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-112-functions-of-a-complex-variable-fall-2008/pages/lecture-notes/). Fall 2008 lecture notes.

ca.cr.title: Cauchy–Riemann equations
ca.cr.define: The real differential of a holomorphic function is complex linear.
ca.cr.statement: For $f=u+iv$ with real $C^1$ components, holomorphy is equivalent to $u_x=v_y$ and $u_y=-v_x$. Equivalently, $\partial_{\bar z}f=0$.
ca.cr.hypotheses: The sufficient condition here assumes continuous first partial derivatives on an open set.
ca.cr.caution: Pointwise equations without regularity are not the stated sufficient criterion.
ca.cr.proof_idea: Identify the real differential with multiplication by a complex number.
ca.cr.references:
CA: analytic functions.

- **CA** — Sigurdur Helgason; notes by Hongxi Wang. [MIT 18.112: Functions of a Complex Variable](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-112-functions-of-a-complex-variable-fall-2008/pages/lecture-notes/). Fall 2008 lecture notes.

ca.series.title: Power series and analyticity
ca.series.define: A complex power series converges locally uniformly inside its radius of convergence and may be differentiated termwise there. Holomorphic functions locally equal their Taylor series.
ca.series.statement: A complex power series converges locally uniformly inside its radius of convergence and may be differentiated termwise there. Holomorphic functions locally equal their Taylor series.
ca.series.hypotheses: Taylor expansion is inside a disk contained in the domain of holomorphy.
ca.series.caution: Real smoothness does not imply analyticity; boundary convergence needs a separate argument.
ca.series.proof_idea: Use uniform convergence on smaller disks and Cauchy estimates for the Taylor remainder.
ca.series.prerequisites:
**Within this subject**

- [Cauchy integral formula](./notes/ca.cauchy-formula.md)

**From other subjects**

- [Uniform convergence](./notes/ra.uniform.md) — Real analysis
ca.series.references:
CA: power series; Cauchy formula.

- **CA** — Sigurdur Helgason; notes by Hongxi Wang. [MIT 18.112: Functions of a Complex Variable](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-112-functions-of-a-complex-variable-fall-2008/pages/lecture-notes/). Fall 2008 lecture notes.

ca.contours.title: Contour integrals and winding number
ca.contours.define: Winding number measures the signed turns of a closed contour around a point.
ca.contours.statement: For a piecewise $C^1$ closed curve $\gamma$ and $a$ off its image, $\operatorname{Ind}(\gamma,a)=(2\pi i)^{-1}\int_\gamma dz/(z-a)$ is an integer.
ca.contours.hypotheses: Orientation and the parametrized curve, including repeated traversal, matter.
ca.contours.example: A positively oriented circle winds once around its center and zero times around an exterior point.
ca.contours.caution: Being geometrically enclosed is inadequate for self-intersecting or multiply traversed curves.
ca.contours.references:
CA: line integrals; general Cauchy theorem.

- **CA** — Sigurdur Helgason; notes by Hongxi Wang. [MIT 18.112: Functions of a Complex Variable](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-112-functions-of-a-complex-variable-fall-2008/pages/lecture-notes/). Fall 2008 lecture notes.

ca.cauchy.title: Cauchy–Goursat theorem
ca.cauchy.define: Holomorphic functions have zero closed-contour integrals on simply connected domains.
ca.cauchy.statement: If $f$ is holomorphic on a simply connected domain $U$, then $\int_\gamma f(z)\,dz=0$ for every closed piecewise $C^1$ curve in $U$.
ca.cauchy.hypotheses: The entire curve lies in the domain. Holomorphy does not require an a priori continuous derivative.
ca.cauchy.example: The integral of $1/z$ around the unit circle is nonzero because the punctured plane is not simply connected.
ca.cauchy.caution: The general homological version requires a null-homologous cycle in the domain.
ca.cauchy.proof_idea: Prove the triangle theorem by subdivision, then construct primitives locally and use simple connectivity.
ca.cauchy.prerequisites:
**Within this subject**

- [Contour integrals and winding number](./notes/ca.contours.md)
ca.cauchy.references:
CA: Cauchy–Goursat; general Cauchy theorem.

- **CA** — Sigurdur Helgason; notes by Hongxi Wang. [MIT 18.112: Functions of a Complex Variable](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-112-functions-of-a-complex-variable-fall-2008/pages/lecture-notes/). Fall 2008 lecture notes.

ca.cauchy-formula.title: Cauchy integral formula
ca.cauchy-formula.define: Boundary values recover all interior derivatives of a holomorphic function.
ca.cauchy-formula.statement: If $f$ is holomorphic near a closed disk and $z$ is interior, then $f^{(n)}(z)=\frac{n!}{2\pi i}\int_{\partial D}\frac{f(\zeta)}{(\zeta-z)^{n+1}}\,d\zeta$.
ca.cauchy-formula.hypotheses: The circle is positively oriented; $n$ is a nonnegative integer.
ca.cauchy-formula.example: On a radius-$R$ circle about $z$, $|f^{(n)}(z)|\le n!\max_{\partial D}|f|/R^n$.
ca.cauchy-formula.caution: The evaluation point must stay off the integration curve.
ca.cauchy-formula.proof_idea: Apply Cauchy's theorem after removing a small disk around the evaluation point, then differentiate under the integral.
ca.cauchy-formula.references:
CA: special Cauchy formula and applications.

- **CA** — Sigurdur Helgason; notes by Hongxi Wang. [MIT 18.112: Functions of a Complex Variable](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-112-functions-of-a-complex-variable-fall-2008/pages/lecture-notes/). Fall 2008 lecture notes.

ca.identity.title: Identity theorem
ca.identity.define: Two holomorphic functions on a connected domain coincide if their agreement set has an accumulation point in that domain.
ca.identity.statement: Two holomorphic functions on a connected domain coincide if their agreement set has an accumulation point in that domain.
ca.identity.hypotheses: The accumulation point is interior, and the domain is connected.
ca.identity.example: A holomorphic function vanishing on a real interval inside its domain is identically zero.
ca.identity.caution: Zeros may accumulate at a boundary point without forcing global vanishing.
ca.identity.proof_idea: The first nonzero Taylor coefficient makes a zero isolated; propagate equality across the connected domain.
ca.identity.references:
CA: local properties of analytic functions.

- **CA** — Sigurdur Helgason; notes by Hongxi Wang. [MIT 18.112: Functions of a Complex Variable](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-112-functions-of-a-complex-variable-fall-2008/pages/lecture-notes/). Fall 2008 lecture notes.

ca.liouville.title: Liouville and the fundamental theorem of algebra
ca.liouville.define: Every bounded entire function is constant. Consequently every nonconstant complex polynomial has a complex root.
ca.liouville.statement: Every bounded entire function is constant. Consequently every nonconstant complex polynomial has a complex root.
ca.liouville.hypotheses: Boundedness is global on the entire complex plane.
ca.liouville.example: If a polynomial had no zero, its reciprocal would be entire and bounded.
ca.liouville.caution: A bounded holomorphic function on a proper domain need not be constant.
ca.liouville.proof_idea: Let the radius in the first-derivative Cauchy estimate tend to infinity.
ca.liouville.references:
CA: Cauchy estimates.

- **CA** — Sigurdur Helgason; notes by Hongxi Wang. [MIT 18.112: Functions of a Complex Variable](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-112-functions-of-a-complex-variable-fall-2008/pages/lecture-notes/). Fall 2008 lecture notes.
ca.liouville.notes: [Liouville and the fundamental theorem of algebra](./notes/ca.liouville.md)

ca.maximum.title: Maximum modulus principle
ca.maximum.define: A nonconstant holomorphic function on a connected domain cannot have a local interior maximum of its modulus.
ca.maximum.statement: A nonconstant holomorphic function on a connected domain cannot have a local interior maximum of its modulus.
ca.maximum.hypotheses: The maximized quantity is the modulus, not an ordering of complex values.
ca.maximum.example: For a function continuous on a closed disk and holomorphic inside, its maximum modulus is attained on the boundary.
ca.maximum.caution: The boundary conclusion requires compactness and continuous extension to the boundary.
ca.maximum.proof_idea: Use the mean-value identity and its equality case, or the local power-series expansion.
ca.maximum.references:
CA: local mapping; maximum modulus.

- **CA** — Sigurdur Helgason; notes by Hongxi Wang. [MIT 18.112: Functions of a Complex Variable](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-112-functions-of-a-complex-variable-fall-2008/pages/lecture-notes/). Fall 2008 lecture notes.

ca.singularities.title: Laurent series and isolated singularities
ca.singularities.define: An isolated singularity is removable, a pole, or essential according to whether the Laurent principal part is zero, finite nonzero, or infinite.
ca.singularities.statement: An isolated singularity is removable, a pole, or essential according to whether the Laurent principal part is zero, finite nonzero, or infinite.
ca.singularities.hypotheses: The function is holomorphic on a punctured disk.
ca.singularities.example: $\sin z/z$, $1/z^2$, and $e^{1/z}$ illustrate the three cases at zero.
ca.singularities.caution: A branch point such as zero for a logarithm is not an isolated singularity of a single-valued holomorphic function on a punctured disk.
ca.singularities.references:
CA: isolated singularities; Laurent series.

- **CA** — Sigurdur Helgason; notes by Hongxi Wang. [MIT 18.112: Functions of a Complex Variable](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-112-functions-of-a-complex-variable-fall-2008/pages/lecture-notes/). Fall 2008 lecture notes.

ca.residues.title: Residue theorem
ca.residues.define: Contour integrals of meromorphic functions reduce to weighted residues at poles.
ca.residues.statement: For a meromorphic function with finitely many poles relevant to a null-homologous contour, $\int_\gamma f\,dz=2\pi i\sum_a\operatorname{Ind}(\gamma,a)\operatorname{Res}_a f$.
ca.residues.hypotheses: The contour avoids poles and is null-homologous in the original domain before removing them.
ca.residues.example: The residue of $g(z)/(z-a)$ is $g(a)$ when $g$ is holomorphic near $a$.
ca.residues.caution: Higher-order poles require the Laurent coefficient, not simply the numerator value.
ca.residues.proof_idea: Subtract principal parts and apply Cauchy's theorem to the remaining holomorphic function.
ca.residues.prerequisites:
**Within this subject**

- [Laurent series and isolated singularities](./notes/ca.singularities.md)
- [Contour integrals and winding number](./notes/ca.contours.md)
ca.residues.references:
CA: residue theorem.

- **CA** — Sigurdur Helgason; notes by Hongxi Wang. [MIT 18.112: Functions of a Complex Variable](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-112-functions-of-a-complex-variable-fall-2008/pages/lecture-notes/). Fall 2008 lecture notes.

ca.argument.title: Argument principle
ca.argument.define: The winding of function values counts interior zeros minus poles.
ca.argument.statement: For a positively oriented Jordan boundary, $(2\pi i)^{-1}\int f'/f$ equals the number of zeros minus poles inside, counted with multiplicity.
ca.argument.hypotheses: The Jordan boundary is piecewise C1. The function is meromorphic near the enclosed closed region and has no zero or pole on the boundary.
ca.argument.example: A zero of order $m$ contributes residue $m$ to $f'/f$.
ca.argument.caution: Zeros on the contour invalidate the formula without an additional limiting prescription.
ca.argument.proof_idea: Compute the local residues of the logarithmic derivative.
ca.argument.references:
CA: argument principle.

- **CA** — Sigurdur Helgason; notes by Hongxi Wang. [MIT 18.112: Functions of a Complex Variable](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-112-functions-of-a-complex-variable-fall-2008/pages/lecture-notes/). Fall 2008 lecture notes.

ca.rouche.title: Rouché's theorem
ca.rouche.define: A strict boundary perturbation bound preserves the number of interior zeros.
ca.rouche.statement: If $f,g$ are holomorphic near a closed Jordan region and $|g|<|f|$ on its boundary, then $f$ and $f+g$ have the same number of interior zeros.
ca.rouche.hypotheses: Zeros are counted with multiplicity; the strict boundary inequality is the stated version.
ca.rouche.example: On $|z|=2$, $z^5$ dominates $z+1$, so $z^5+z+1$ has five zeros inside.
ca.rouche.caution: The theorem counts zeros but does not locate individual roots.
ca.rouche.proof_idea: The boundary functions $f+tg$ avoid zero, so their winding number is constant for $0\le t\le1$.
ca.rouche.references:
CA: Rouché theorem.

- **CA** — Sigurdur Helgason; notes by Hongxi Wang. [MIT 18.112: Functions of a Complex Variable](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-112-functions-of-a-complex-variable-fall-2008/pages/lecture-notes/). Fall 2008 lecture notes.

ca.schwarz.title: Schwarz lemma
ca.schwarz.define: A disk self-map fixing zero contracts radial size, with rigid equality cases.
ca.schwarz.statement: For holomorphic $f:\mathbb D\to\mathbb D$ with $f(0)=0$, $|f(z)|\le|z|$ and $|f'(0)|\le1$. Equality at a nonzero point, or in the derivative bound, forces a rotation.
ca.schwarz.hypotheses: The normalization at zero is essential to this form.
ca.schwarz.caution: For general disk maps use automorphisms and Schwarz–Pick, not the unnormalized inequality.
ca.schwarz.proof_idea: Apply the maximum principle to the removable extension of $f(z)/z$.
ca.schwarz.references:
CA: Schwarz lemma.

- **CA** — Sigurdur Helgason; notes by Hongxi Wang. [MIT 18.112: Functions of a Complex Variable](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-112-functions-of-a-complex-variable-fall-2008/pages/lecture-notes/). Fall 2008 lecture notes.

ca.normal.title: Montel's theorem
ca.normal.define: A locally uniformly bounded family of holomorphic functions on a plane domain has a subsequence converging uniformly on compact subsets from every sequence in the family.
ca.normal.statement: A locally uniformly bounded family of holomorphic functions on a plane domain has a subsequence converging uniformly on compact subsets from every sequence in the family.
ca.normal.hypotheses: The locally bounded version yields a finite holomorphic limit; the compact-open topology is intended.
ca.normal.example: Holomorphic disk maps with values in $\mathbb D$ form a normal family.
ca.normal.caution: Pointwise boundedness is not the hypothesis, and meromorphic normality uses the spherical metric.
ca.normal.proof_idea: Cauchy estimates give equicontinuity on compact subsets; apply compactness and a diagonal exhaustion.
ca.normal.prerequisites:
**Within this subject**

- [Cauchy integral formula](./notes/ca.cauchy-formula.md)

**From other subjects**

- [Arzelà–Ascoli theorem](./notes/ra.ascoli.md) — Real analysis
ca.normal.references:
CA: normal families.

- **CA** — Sigurdur Helgason; notes by Hongxi Wang. [MIT 18.112: Functions of a Complex Variable](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-112-functions-of-a-complex-variable-fall-2008/pages/lecture-notes/). Fall 2008 lecture notes.

ca.riemann-mapping.title: Riemann mapping theorem
ca.riemann-mapping.define: Proper simply connected plane domains are conformally equivalent to the disk.
ca.riemann-mapping.statement: Every nonempty simply connected proper plane domain is biholomorphic to $\mathbb D$. Specifying an interior image of zero and a positive real derivative fixes the normalized inverse map uniquely.
ca.riemann-mapping.hypotheses: The domain is open, connected, simply connected, and different from the whole plane.
ca.riemann-mapping.example: The upper half-plane is mapped to the disk by a Möbius transformation.
ca.riemann-mapping.caution: The theorem does not by itself assert continuous extension to an arbitrary boundary.
ca.riemann-mapping.proof_idea: Optimize a normalized univalent family using normality; a missing image point would permit an improving map.
ca.riemann-mapping.references:
CA: Riemann mapping theorem.

- **CA** — Sigurdur Helgason; notes by Hongxi Wang. [MIT 18.112: Functions of a Complex Variable](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-112-functions-of-a-complex-variable-fall-2008/pages/lecture-notes/). Fall 2008 lecture notes.

ca.continuation.title: Analytic continuation and monodromy
ca.continuation.define: Local holomorphic germs continue uniquely along a fixed chain where overlaps agree. If a germ can be continued along every path in a simply connected domain, monodromy makes the continuation single-valued.
ca.continuation.statement: Local holomorphic germs continue uniquely along a fixed chain where overlaps agree. If a germ can be continued along every path in a simply connected domain, monodromy makes the continuation single-valued.
ca.continuation.hypotheses: Continuation along all paths is an extra existence assumption, not a consequence of simple connectivity alone.
ca.continuation.example: Continuing a logarithm around zero changes its value by an integer multiple of $2\pi i$.
ca.continuation.caution: Uniqueness on overlaps does not eliminate monodromy in a multiply connected domain.
ca.continuation.proof_idea: Use the identity theorem and deform path chains through a homotopy.
ca.continuation.prerequisites:
**Within this subject**

- [Identity theorem](./notes/ca.identity.md)

**From other subjects**

- [Homotopies and homotopy equivalence](./notes/tp.homotopy.md) — Topology
ca.continuation.references:
CA: analytic continuation; CM: Riemann surfaces.

- **CA** — Sigurdur Helgason; notes by Hongxi Wang. [MIT 18.112: Functions of a Complex Variable](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-112-functions-of-a-complex-variable-fall-2008/pages/lecture-notes/). Fall 2008 lecture notes.
- **CM** — John M. Lee. [Introduction to Complex Manifolds](https://sites.math.washington.edu/~lee/Books/ICM/). Author's book page.

ca.harmonic.title: Harmonic functions and conjugates
ca.harmonic.define: Harmonic functions on simply connected plane domains admit global conjugates.
ca.harmonic.statement: Real and imaginary parts of a holomorphic function are harmonic. A real $C^2$ harmonic function on a simply connected plane domain is the real part of a holomorphic function.
ca.harmonic.hypotheses: The global conjugate conclusion requires the stated topological condition.
ca.harmonic.example: $\log|z|$ is harmonic off zero but has no global single-valued harmonic conjugate on $\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}$.
ca.harmonic.caution: Harmonicity is a real second-order condition; holomorphy is a complex first-order condition.
ca.harmonic.proof_idea: The Cauchy–Riemann equations define a closed differential form whose periods vanish on a simply connected domain.
ca.harmonic.references:
CA: harmonic functions.

- **CA** — Sigurdur Helgason; notes by Hongxi Wang. [MIT 18.112: Functions of a Complex Variable](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-112-functions-of-a-complex-variable-fall-2008/pages/lecture-notes/). Fall 2008 lecture notes.

ca.riemann-surfaces.title: Riemann surfaces
ca.riemann-surfaces.define: A Riemann surface is a connected, Hausdorff, second-countable complex manifold of complex dimension one, with holomorphic coordinate transitions.
ca.riemann-surfaces.statement: A Riemann surface is a connected, Hausdorff, second-countable complex manifold of complex dimension one, with holomorphic coordinate transitions.
ca.riemann-surfaces.hypotheses: The topology and complex atlas are part of the structure.
ca.riemann-surfaces.example: The Riemann sphere and complex tori $\mathbb C/\Lambda$ are compact examples.
ca.riemann-surfaces.caution: A topological surface may carry many inequivalent conformal structures; compact does not mean biholomorphic to the sphere.
ca.riemann-surfaces.prerequisites:
**Within this subject**

- [Analytic continuation and monodromy](./notes/ca.continuation.md)

**From other subjects**

- [Topological manifolds](./notes/tp.manifolds.md) — Topology
ca.riemann-surfaces.references:
CM: complex manifolds and Riemann surfaces.

- **CM** — John M. Lee. [Introduction to Complex Manifolds](https://sites.math.washington.edu/~lee/Books/ICM/). Author's book page.

ca.mittag-leffler.title: Mittag–Leffler theorem
ca.mittag-leffler.define: On a plane domain, arbitrary prescribed finite principal parts at a discrete set of points are realized by a meromorphic function with no other poles.
ca.mittag-leffler.statement: On a plane domain, arbitrary prescribed finite principal parts at a discrete set of points are realized by a meromorphic function with no other poles.
ca.mittag-leffler.hypotheses: The prescribed set has no accumulation point inside the domain.
ca.mittag-leffler.example: Prescribing simple poles with residue one at the integers leads to meromorphic partial-fraction constructions.
ca.mittag-leffler.caution: On compact Riemann surfaces analogous prescriptions have global obstructions; unrestricted plane-domain existence does not transfer.
ca.mittag-leffler.proof_idea: Correct successive finite sums by holomorphic approximants to obtain convergence on compact exhaustions.
ca.mittag-leffler.prerequisites:
**Within this subject**

- [Laurent series and isolated singularities](./notes/ca.singularities.md)
- [Montel's theorem](./notes/ca.normal.md)
ca.mittag-leffler.references:
CA: Mittag–Leffler theorem.

- **CA** — Sigurdur Helgason; notes by Hongxi Wang. [MIT 18.112: Functions of a Complex Variable](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-112-functions-of-a-complex-variable-fall-2008/pages/lecture-notes/). Fall 2008 lecture notes.
